key_insight: The paper argues that LLM-assisted manuscript writing should be verified with deterministic, stage-by-stage integrity gates whenever possible, rather than relying only on self-critique or a single reviewer prompt.
clinical_relevance: For clinical research workflows, this approach could reduce hidden errors in citations, numbers, and reporting-checklist compliance before a manuscript is submitted.
method: Split manuscript preparation into modular skills.
Add halt-on-failure verification gates at each stage transition.
Use deterministic checks first, and only use prose-based review when interpretation is unavoidable.
evidence_signal: In evaluation across STARD, PRISMA, and STROBE pipelines, the system’s deterministic gates verified clean manifests and detected all 27 injected defects with no false positives on matched clean fixtures.
watch_item: This is an infrastructure and verification approach, not proof of higher manuscript quality in general, and it still depends on correct implementation of the underlying checks and source data.
paper_title: Deterministic Integrity Gates for LLM-Assisted Clinical Manuscript Preparation: An Auditable Biomedical Informatics Architecture
